entries.title: Numbers 22:1
segments:
The plains of Moab; in the Jordan valley; so called because they had once belonged to Moab.  They had afterwards been taken by the Amorites, and now by the children of Israel. 
 
  This side; the east side of Jordan. 
 
  Jericho; a city of Canaan on the west side of Jordan.

entries.title: Numbers 22:3
segments: Those who know not Jehovah and do not trust in him, are always exposed to distressing fears, and to many evils from which no human wisdom or power can save them.

entries.title: Numbers 22:4
segments: Elders; the word translated elders means also princes or rulers.
Midian; a people living near the Moabites, and who on this occasion acted in concert with the Moabites,

. 
 
  Lick up all; overcome and swallow us up.

entries.title: Numbers 22:5
segments: Balaam; a noted sorcerer or soothsayer, of Mesopotamia.
Pethor; a place near the Euphrates.

entries.title: Numbers 22:6
segments:
Wot; know. 
 
The wicked place that confidence in men which should be placed only in God, and hope for that from them which can come only from him.

entries.title: Numbers 22:7
segments: Rewards of divination; money or presents to induce him to come and curse Israel.

entries.title: Numbers 22:8
segments: As the Lord shall speak; this shows that Balaam had some knowledge of Jehovah, and of his obligations to follow his guidance.

entries.title: Numbers 22:9
segments:
God came unto Balaam; whether he had ever done this before we are not informed. 
 
God has sometimes held communications with wicked men, and given them a knowledge of his will.  But knowledge alone, without love, will not lead them so to obey him as to obtain his blessing.

entries.title: Numbers 22:12
segments: All whom god blesses will in the end be truly blessed; and all whom he curses, will in the end be wretched.

entries.title: Numbers 22:13
segments: Refuseth to give me leave; the Lord not only did this, but told Balaam not to go.

entries.title: Numbers 22:17
segments: Those who supremely regard this world often think that other men, like themselves, for a sufficient reward, can be persuaded to do what they wish.

entries.title: Numbers 22:18
segments: I cannot go beyond the word of the Lord; it was true that he could not, consistently with his duty, though it seems he earnestly desired to do so.

entries.title: Numbers 22:19
segments: To love the reward of iniquity and desire to do wrong to obtain it, is exceedingly dangerous.  It exposes men to be given up to the practice of iniquity till they sink into irremediable ruin.

entries.title: Numbers 22:20
segments: Rise up, and go with them; in this, God suffered.  Balaam, from the love of unrighteous gain, to follow his own inclinations. 2Pe 2.13-16

entries.title: Numbers 22:22
segments: Because he went; Balaam's object and course were wrong and displeasing to God.
The angel of the Lord; supposed to be the same which spoke to him,
, and who is spoken of,

entries.title: Numbers 22:27
segments: Men are often angry with dumb beasts and cruelly beat them, when the fault is all in themselves.

entries.title: Numbers 22:30
segments: God could speak through the mouths of dumb animals, and cause them to tell a tale which would make the hearts of their owners quake with fear, and show that, through sin, man has sunk below the beasts that perish.

entries.title: Numbers 22:33
segments: Beasts sometimes see what men do not, and by doing that for which they are abused, save their owners from death.

entries.title: Numbers 22:34
segments: To have God for an adversary is an unspeakable calamity, and one that should by all needful sacrifices and labors be avoided.

entries.title: Numbers 22:36
segments: Utmost coast; boundary of his kingdom.

entries.title: Numbers 22:39
segments: Kirjath-huzoth; meaning, a city of streets; probably of many streets--a large city.

entries.title: Numbers 22:40
segments:
Balak offered oxen; as is supposed, to his idols. 
 
  Sent to Balaam; to come and feast on the sacrifice.

entries.title: Numbers 22:41
segments:
Baal; an idol worshipped by many eastern nations. 
 
All expectations from men, in opposition to the purposes and will of God, are vain, and will end in disappointment.
